timing-before: timing "before": an object trigger fires AFTER the change is committed, so a rule that runs before the write — and can still change or refuse it — has nothing to fire on.
timing-default: timing "before": an object trigger fires AFTER the change is committed, so a rule that runs before the write — and can still change or refuse it — has nothing to fire on.
conditions-scalar: conditions: the rule stores a integer where a JsonLogic expression tree is expected, so there is nothing the switch could evaluate.
conditions-sub-scope: conditions use the sub-scope operator(s) some, which rebind what "var" means inside them. Rewriting request paths to item paths through one of those would be wrong exactly where it looked right, so it is refused rather than guessed.

conditions read "id": an object event carries the object and nothing else — no request, no headers, no query — so only "body" paths have an equivalent. Dropping the rest would make this rule fire on every object instead of some.
conditions-request-paths: conditions read "headers.x-api-key", "query.page": an object event carries the object and nothing else — no request, no headers, no query — so only "body" paths have an equivalent. Dropping the rest would make this rule fire on every object instead of some.
conditions-both: conditions use the sub-scope operator(s) all, which rebind what "var" means inside them. Rewriting request paths to item paths through one of those would be wrong exactly where it looked right, so it is refused rather than guessed.

type-envelope: type "mapping": this rule kind acts on the request/response envelope, and an object event has no envelope to act on — no step reproduces it. The kinds with an object-event equivalent are "synchronization" and "flow".
type-missing: type "": this rule kind acts on the request/response envelope, and an object event has no envelope to act on — no step reproduces it. The kinds with an object-event equivalent are "synchronization" and "flow".
